title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol: secret decree Rom. 9 — in God no prior/posterior decrees; order of causes
pass_a_gloss: Solution. I answer, Provided that secret decree of God be conceded, of him whose he wills he has mercy, and whom he wills leaving to their innate hardness, loving Jacob, having Esau in hatred, and that before all consideration of things well or ill done in the same, we labor not even a little about the order of priority and posteriority in the decree of eternal life and of efficacious grace as to the predestinated themselves. For we know that in God as to the thing there are not decrees some prior or posterior to others: but as to the mode of our consideration and the mutual habitude of things the same decree compared to another can be both prior and posterior to it, according to a diverse order of causes. Thus the decree of giving faith in the order of efficient cause is prior to that of giving life: the decree of giving life in the order of final cause is prior to that of giving faith.
pass_b_english: Sol. I answer: grant that secret decree of God who has mercy on whom he wills and leaves whom he wills to their innate hardness — loving Jacob, hating Esau, before any consideration of their good or evil deeds — and we do not labor even a little over priority and posteriority in the decree of eternal life and efficacious grace as to the predestinated. In God as to the thing, decrees are not prior or posterior to each other; as to our mode of considering and the mutual relation of things, the same decree compared to another can be both prior and posterior by a diverse order of causes. So the decree to give faith is prior in the order of efficient cause to giving life; the decree to give life is prior in the order of final cause to giving faith.
source_text: Sol. Respondeo, Modo concedatur arcanum illud decretum Dei, cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult duritiae suae innatae relinquentes, Jacobum diligentis, Esavum odio habentis, idque ante omnem considerationem bene aut male factorum in iisdem, nos de ordine prioritatis et posterioritatis in decreto aeternae vitae et efficacis gratiae quoad ipsos praedestinatos, ne tantillum quidem laborare. Nam scimus in Deo quoad rem non esse decreta alia aliis priora aut posteriora: quoad modum autem considerationis nostrae et rerum inter se habitudinem idem decretum alteri comparatum potest eo et prius et posterius esse, secundum diversum ordinem causarum. Sic decretum dandi fidem in ordine causae efficientis prius est quam dandi vitam: decretum dandi vitam in ordine causae finalis prius est quam dandi fidem.
